Connect to a Spark Connect server

spark_connect.Rd

spark_connect() opens a session on a Spark Connect endpoint: it builds the gRPC channel the connection string describes, proves it with one Config call and one SparkVersion call, and refuses servers older than Spark 3.5.0. spark_disconnect() releases the session on the server and closes the channel.

Usage

spark_connect(
  url = Sys.getenv("SPARK_REMOTE"),
  ...,
  user_id = NULL,
  session_id = NULL,
  user_agent = NULL,
  headers = NULL,
  deadline = NULL
)

spark_disconnect(con, allow_reconnect = FALSE)

Arguments

url

A connection string, sc://host:port/;param=value;.... It defaults to the SPARK_REMOTE environment variable. The default port is 15002. The reserved parameters are token (a bearer token; it turns TLS on, except to localhost without use_ssl), use_ssl, user_id, user_agent, session_id, grpc_max_message_size, grpc_keepalive_enabled, grpc_keepalive_time_ms, grpc_keepalive_timeout_ms and grpc_keepalive_without_calls (accepted and ignored, as PySpark does). Every other parameter is sent as a header on every call.

...

Named parameters appended to url, such as token = "...".

user_id, session_id, user_agent

The user id sent with every call (by default the user_id parameter, then SPARK_USER, then USER), the session's id (a UUID; by default a new version 4 UUID), and the text that starts the client type the server logs (by default SPARK_CONNECT_USER_AGENT, then "zuspark"). Each takes precedence over the parameter of the same name in url.

headers

Extra headers for every call, as a named character vector, for names that are not valid in a URL.

deadline

Seconds each call other than a query may take. The default is 30.

con

A zuspark_connection.

allow_reconnect

If TRUE, the server lets a later connection reuse this session's id. By default the id is retired with the session.

Value

spark_connect() returns a zuspark_connection. spark_disconnect() returns TRUE invisibly, or FALSE if the session was already released.

Examples

con <- spark_connect()
con
#> <zuspark_connection> sc://127.0.0.1:15002 (Spark 4.2.1)
#>   session: b9ba8758-2a2a-47b1-99da-fe915dc56979
spark_disconnect(con)
